correctness.rationale: Using the published split-quadratic Weierstrass form, the 2-torsion ratio lambda=N/D has degree two with six distinct cusp preimages. Direct Legendre formula J(lambda) has five non-cusp branch preimages over j=0 or 1728, so its composite is Belyi exactly for two chosen branch values in this set. Degree-two rational maps with prescribed unordered branch values are unique up to base automorphisms, and anharmonic S3 has exactly three pair-orbits. Quadratic twisting cannot preserve all six I2 fibres unless unramified and hence trivial on P1_C. Exact symbolic polynomial identity and gcd computations from packaged verify_belyi.py check all three representative equations and the three 12-sheet passports, including infinity. Verified limitations exclude abstract-surface isomorphism.

originality.rationale: Ciliberto et al 2026 §2.4 explicitly classify the two-quadratic six-I2 family, but do not classify the Belyi special locus. Earlier research result c87923d7 describes the Humbert condition on singular-fibre positions, while other earlier finding cd0c1113 concerns a different (4,2) j-map. Degree-24 K3 Belyi tables do not imply degree-12 rational Belyi surfaces. Targeted primary-source and published-finding corpus comparisons found no directly equivalent three-orbit/passport theorem; residual older-dessins coverage risks stated, not misrepresented as absent.

value.rationale: Belyi ramification of the canonical j-map is a natural intrinsic invariant of a rational elliptic fibration. Determining its entire finite locus of three fibration-isomorphism classes in a two-parameter family and computing their pairwise-distinct dessins passports gives a complete special-subfamily classification not encoded in the published fibre configuration or two-moduli theorem.
